subject: Clarify: retention windows + BYOK options for Orchard PoC
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@orchardhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orchard Health Security Team <security@orchardhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Retention windows + BYOK options for POC

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. The security team had two quick follow-ups before we sign off on the POC environment: 1) we need a clear statement of the minimum and maximum retention windows Redwood can guarantee for transient logs and per-tenant audit events, and 2) confirmation on BYOK/KMS options during the POC (we need to know what keys we control vs. what Redwood controls, and how key rotation works).

I attached a short PDF with our questionnaire (orchard-retention-questions.pdf). Can someone on your team confirm the answers and indicate whether there are any gating items that would block the POC? We are aiming to start the POC the week of Nov 29, so timing is tight.

Best,
Maya Singh
Security Lead, Orchard Health

---
Attachments: orchard-retention-questions.pdf (1 page PDF)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention windows + BYOK options for POC

Maya — thank you for the questions and for the fast turnaround. Looping in infra/product/security ops so we can give concrete answers and flag any blockers. High level answers below; detailed matrix in the attached spreadsheet (retention-matrix-v2.xlsx).

- Minimum retention: ephemeral request-level logs can be configured to 0 days for PII-sensitive flows, but audit events (auth NIST-level events + access histories) have a minimum enforced retention of 30 days for operational debugging and SLA investigations.
- Maximum retention: hosted customers may request up to 7 years for audit exports; for POC we recommend 13 months as a default unless you need long-term retention — longer windows require legal/compliance review and are subject to storage fees.
- BYOK/KMS during POC: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in the Private deployment and Dedicated with VPC; hosted POC can use a Customer-Managed KMS via a short-lived tokenized key exchange (we maintain the key wrapping service but do not retain plaintext key material). Rotation is supported: policies can be set to auto-rotate every 90/180 days, and we publish rotation events to audit logs.

Open items we still need to triage:
1) Whether Orchard needs an escrowed key copy for legal hold (this is a policy decision).
2) Retention carveouts for ephemeral debug traces created by sampling (we need exact endpoints/feature flags you plan to use).

Marissa/Ben/Kimberly — can you review the matrix and flag any technical blockers or timelines? I suggested a short internal sync Monday morning.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: retention-matrix-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention windows + BYOK options for POC

Thanks Jordan — I pulled the matrix into product/ops context and added a few rows describing implementation effort and gating items. Quick notes:

- Audit events: we can expose per-tenant retention controls in the Console for Dedicated/Private by end of Q1; for hosted POC we can expose a limited self-serve TTL UI (30/90/365 days) by early-December if we prioritize it. Backend work is small but we need a short security review for the TTL UI.
- BYOK: Private + Dedicated: full BYOK where customer supplies a KMS ARN works today. Hosted: we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS via a mediated exchange (you keep control of the CMK in your cloud account; Redwood uses a service account to perform envelope encryption). This is available but requires 1) KMS policy updates on your side and 2) a short runbook to validate access.
- Rotation events: we emit rotation metadata to audit logs, but we currently do not ship a rotation certificate by default — we can add that as an add-on (low effort).

Blocking questions for the Orchard security team: do you need a written attestation that Redwood never stores plaintext keys? Also confirm whether ephemeral traces can be sampled at all (if no, we need to remove sampling instrumentation for the POC).

I attached two example rows in the retention matrix and a proposed timeline.

- Marissa
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: retention-matrix-v2.xlsx (updated)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@orchardhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention windows + BYOK options for POC

Maya — quick follow-up from infra/security side. A few concrete asks we can action this week to keep you on schedule:

1) If Orchard can confirm the minimum retention selection (30 vs. 90 days) for the POC, infra will provision ephemeral buckets with that TTL and provide the config snippet we use on the customer side.
2) For BYOK: please provide the KMS principal (ARN) you'll use in the POC and a contact to coordinate the temporary KMS policy change. We will not accept key material; exchange is envelope-based.
3) We will provide a signed statement (PDF) that Redwood does not retain plaintext CMKs for hosted POCs. If you need additional legal language, send a redline and we can route to Legal.

Action items: Jordan to schedule 30-min sync Monday (Nov 23) EOD PST; Orchard to send KMS principal and minimal retention choice.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
